about: The differences between each framed fixture's figure and its golden frame that are allowed, each with its reason. Compared by equality in both directions by design-fixtures T1.7 and T1.8; re-derived by `npx tsx tools/design/figures.ts --write`, which keeps a reason only while its entry keeps its kind. See DESIGN_FIXTURES.md §The figure.

differences.reason: The figure is a whole agent session; the frame is the framework's small harness application with one settled call and one running stream. Figure-only: the figure's session chrome (`✦` model, `⎇` branch, `✎`, `»` posture) is the application's chrome, which the harness's two-line chrome does not draw; `▹` a reasoning head, `◼ ◻` a todo list and `−`, `⋯` and `▌` of an edit's diff and the caret are the agent's content — the framework has the call head, the `⎿` body and the stream block, which the frame shows. Frame-only: `⇥ ⇧ ⏎` are the footer's key hints (`⏎ send  ⇧⏎ newline  ⇥ complete`), which the framework draws and the figure's footer does not carry; `│` is the continuation gutter under `⎿`, which the registry draws blank (ruling 2, I4 — b5-dshell's lane owns the change; this entry empties when its goldens move); `⠋` is the running head's braille spinner where the figure's `✦` is the agent set, which is the application's choice of set

The figure is an idle agent session; the frame is the same harness with every head settled. Figure-only: the figure's session chrome (`✦` model, `⎇` branch, `✎`, `»` posture) is the application's chrome, which the harness's two-line chrome does not draw; `█ ░` is the context meter in the status line and `·` the footer's separators, both the application's chrome. Frame-only: `⇥ ⇧ ⏎` are the footer's key hints (`⏎ send  ⇧⏎ newline  ⇥ complete`), which the framework draws and the figure's footer does not carry; `│` is the continuation gutter under `⎿`, which the registry draws blank (ruling 2, I4 — b5-dshell's lane owns the change; this entry empties when its goldens move)

The figure's cancelled head is an edit with a diff, a stopped notice and a todo list; the frame's is a cancelled stream whose block stays and whose `⊘ Cancelled.` is the framework's. Figure-only: `↺` revert, `▲` stopped notice, `◻` todo and `⋯ −` diff content are the agent's; `✦` is its spinner. Frame-only: `⇥ ⇧ ⏎` are the footer's key hints (`⏎ send  ⇧⏎ newline  ⇥ complete`), which the framework draws and the figure's footer does not carry; `│` is the continuation gutter under `⎿`, which the registry draws blank (ruling 2, I4 — b5-dshell's lane owns the change; this entry empties when its goldens move); `█ ░` is the stream's progress bar; `⊘` is the cancelled state's body mark; `❯` is the echo

The frame is the registry's canonical set read through its homes (F1465), so every mark the figure's table draws is in it. The one difference is the em dash of the figure's prose line (`supporting registered marks — inventory-checked`), which the frame words differently

The figure's entries are a model's prose and a head with a count; the frame is two echoed commands and their entries. Figure-only: `·` and `—` are the model's prose and the head's separators at the figure's own slot. Frame-only: `⇥ ⇧ ⏎` are the footer's key hints (`⏎ send  ⇧⏎ newline  ⇥ complete`), which the framework draws and the figure's footer does not carry; `⎿` and `─` are the result hook and the prompt rules; `│` is the continuation gutter under `⎿`, which the registry draws blank (ruling 2, I4 — b5-dshell's lane owns the change; this entry empties when its goldens move)

The figure draws a counted queue band above the prompt; the framework's queue is the entry (`queued behind <verb>`, C23 I5), so there is no band, no `⌥↑ edit the last` and no `⌥⌫` hint in the frame — owed as a design question, not a golden. Figure-only: `↑ ⌥ ⌫` are those hints; `▌` the caret, `◻` a todo and `✦` the agent's spinner. Frame-only: `⇥ ⇧ ⏎` are the footer's key hints (`⏎ send  ⇧⏎ newline  ⇥ complete`), which the framework draws and the figure's footer does not carry; `⠋` the running head's spinner

The figure's startup is an application's welcome (version, endpoint, posture hint, a resumed-session line); the frame is the framework's bare opening with only the prompt, rules and footer, because the harness's application declares no greeting. Figure-only: `· — ⌥ ⎇ ⎿ ▌ ● ✦` are that welcome's content. Frame-only: `⇧` of the footer's `⇧⏎ newline`

The chip's own form agrees (`[parse.ts · 184L]`, painted and bracketed). The figure draws the whole @ completion around it — the menu (› ↑ ↓ ⏎ ⇥), the prompt's rules and caret (─ ❯ ▌) and the size warning (▲), which is M15's question work; the frame's │ is the measuring box's edge

The figure's transient feedback is a footer notice (`copied 47 lines`), a table row and a revert head; the frame shows the footer notice `✓ copied 1 line` and the entry it copied. Figure-only: `▸ ↺ −` and `»` are the table row, the revert head and the posture, which are the application's. Frame-only: `✓` is the copy notice's mark where the figure's footer draws none; `⇥ ⇧ ⏎` are the footer's key hints (`⏎ send  ⇧⏎ newline  ⇥ complete`), which the framework draws and the figure's footer does not carry; `⎿ │ ─ ❯` are the entry's hook and gutter and the rules and prompt

The figure is a settled call whose result is a file list with `⏎ review  d full diff  ↺ revert all`; the frame is a patch result, the framework's nearest built shape. Figure-only: `↺ −` are the revert affordance and delta, the application's. Frame-only: `⇥ ⇧ ⏎` are the footer's key hints (`⏎ send  ⇧⏎ newline  ⇥ complete`), which the framework draws and the figure's footer does not carry; `⋯` is the patch's unchanged-lines residue; `─` the hunk's rule; `❯` the echo; `│` is the continuation gutter under `⎿`, which the registry draws blank (ruling 2, I4 — b5-dshell's lane owns the change; this entry empties when its goldens move)

The figure lists notification channels and a settled-while-away line; the frame draws the away mark opened and its entries. Figure-only: `• ↓ ⌘ ␇ ⟩` are the channel table's bell, title and key marks, which are prose about the terminal and not a surface. Frame-only: `⇥ ⇧ ⏎` are the footer's key hints (`⏎ send  ⇧⏎ newline  ⇥ complete`), which the framework draws and the figure's footer does not carry; `┌ ┐ └ ┘` is the error box of the failed verb (the figure's model-failure row is the agent's); `┃ ╽` the scrollbar the long transcript earns; `✗` the failure mark in that box; `⌃` of the `⌃end` hint

The frame's sub-captions (`focused on linear — NOT chosen`, `inside — weight and a painted handle`) carry an em dash in the repository's own words; every mark of the figure's control and choice cases (`├ ━ ● ◉ ○ ✓ ✗ ┤`) is in the frame

The figure joins a binding's label and its qualifiers with ` · ` (`copy source · enhanced`); the frame prints the action's name alone. The frame heads each scope with the `rule` block `/help keys` draws (`── prompt — where you are`) where the figure heads it with the bare name. The check the row makes is the grouping and the order, and they agree

The bar's four marks (│ ┃ ╽ ╿) agree. The figure draws the bar beside a call's output (● ⎿ ·) and a boxed log whose count sits in the border (┌ ┐ └ ┘ ─); the frame draws the set as a table and a bare bar beside six lines with its residue row (⋯)

The figure's first range is `● keys · 69 bindings` over `key ⇧⏎ newline · enhanced` rows labelled in words; the frame is the real `/help keys` entry, which draws the action's name (`insertNewline`) and heads each scope with the `rule` block. Figure-only: `←` and `⌘` are bindings further down the listing than the first page the frame shows, and `·` the label–qualifier join. Frame-only: `—` the scope rule's tail text, `⎿ ─ │` the entry's hook, the prompt rule and the gutter, `┃` the scrollbar, `❯` the echo. The order and the grouping, which is what §022 settles, agree and are held by C16 T1.197

The figure is the agent session at 40 columns with its shed order; the frame is the harness at 60 columns, the narrowest a session draws (MIN_COLUMNS), so the figure's 40-column composition is not drawable — measured, a session below 60 draws only the notice (§47's frame). Figure-only: the figure's session chrome (`✦` model, `⎇` branch, `✎`, `»` posture) is the application's chrome, which the harness's two-line chrome does not draw; `◻` todo and `▌` caret. Frame-only: `⇥ ⇧ ⏎` are the footer's key hints (`⏎ send  ⇧⏎ newline  ⇥ complete`), which the framework draws and the figure's footer does not carry; `│` is the continuation gutter under `⎿`, which the registry draws blank (ruling 2, I4 — b5-dshell's lane owns the change; this entry empties when its goldens move); `⠋` the running spinner. The shed order itself is not read by this comparison

The figure draws one collapsed head and one open head with a `│` rail; the frame draws the `tree` kind, the nearest built shape (there is no reasoning kind). The marks agree; the difference is the em dash in the figure's `collapsed — the default` annotation, which is the figure's caption and not a drawn mark

✦ in a fixture is the still of an empty spinner slot (`tools/design/fixtures.ts`, SPINNER_SLOT), and the frame draws the agent set at its tick, `⋅`. The frame reads the foreground as a mask, one row per pass, so the ● head, the ▿ reasoning header, the prompt (❯ ▌ ─) and the elision (…) the figure draws around the trail are not in it

The figure draws the context's meter with a `⏎ breakdown` hint and a segmented legend beneath; the frame draws the bar alone through the `progress` kind. Figure-only: `⏎` the hint, `─ └ ┘` the segment legend's brackets and `▐` its swatches — the segmented context composition is the application's (the tree has no kind for a per-segment legend)

The figure is a pending edit approval with a diff and four choices in one row; the frame is a question with two stacked `[a] approve` / `[d] deny` choices in a `┌ Confirm ┐` panel. This is a real disagreement and is proposed as a finding (NEW-b), not blessed: the design draws the question unboxed with a `⟩` lead, the choices in a row and a muted arrow-key footer; the tree draws a titled box, a `▲` lead and stacked keyed choices. Figure-only: `⟩ ✦ −` and `·`. Frame-only: `• ⎿ │ ┌ ┐ └ ┘ ▲ ❯`

The figure's menu is a status row (`3 of 14 ↑↓ move ⏎ run esc close`) over rows with a muted left description and a ghost remainder in the prompt; the frame's rows are right-aligned descriptions with `+ 16 more` and no ghost. This is I9, b5-menu5's lane (C19 §6), and the entry empties when it lands. Figure-only: `↑ ↓ ↹ ▌ ● ✦ ·`. Frame-only: `⇥` of the footer's hint

The frame is the head-mark ladder by state and the state glyph row (✓ ✗ ⊘); the figure draws the marks in context, with ✦ — the fixtures' still of a spinner slot — in the duration, the prompt's caret (❯ ▌) and heads joined by ` · `

The nine alphabets agree. The figure adds §033's sub-cell table — braille in eighths (⡀ ⡄ ⡆ ⡇ ⣧ ⣷) between │ edges — and a spinner (✦, the fixtures' still) for indeterminate work; the frame's braille row draws only the eighth its fill reaches
✦ is the fixtures' still of a spinner slot, beside the indeterminate case the frame does not draw; · and — are the figure's captions. The bar alphabets agree

Segmented draws posts (▮ ▯) — ruling 32, `R-PRG-002`: discrete steps use posts — where §035's figure draws slant (▰ ▱) for the operation preset. ✦ is the fixtures' spinner still; → is the degradation arrow of the figure's ASCII paragraph, whose `[#][.]` `R-PRG-003` overrules

The figure's bar-carrier row draws slant cells (▰ ▱); the frame draws fills and effects as masks over letters and never draws the carrier's cells. · is the figure's attention-group column; the frame's — is its refused-on-a-span line

The frame draws `pills` — a row of peers that sheds — which is the tree's reading of §042's title; the figure draws knobs: a slider (├ ─ ● ┤), radios, toggles (✓ ✗), a stepper (− ×), a dropdown (▾) and a camera pad (┌ ┐ └ ┘ │ ✛). The slider is `control` (§018, built); segmented, switch and stepper are the kinds §073's row names as absent

The frame draws R-SEL-006's four grounds as masks over one table (▸, cells cut with …). The figure adds the prompt's range (❯), the ▌ selection rail, which is C14's and drawn in the transcript's column 0 rather than by the block, the rows' state marks (● ✗) and the chords (⇧ ⌥)

The figure is a live terminal block with an attached mode, a bordered pty and a settled-while-attached line; the frame is the block's own plain output (`kind: terminal`) with no attach, because attaching needs a child process the golden does not run. Figure-only: `┌ ┐ └ ┘ │ ⌃ ⌥ ⏎ ▌` are the attached box and its hints; `● ✦ ⎿ ─ —` are the head and chrome around it, the application's

The figure draws reverse search as a list of hits with `3 of 214` and `⌥r older`; the frame is the readline-style one-liner `(reverse-i-search) `no': …`. A real disagreement, proposed as NEW-b2 and not blessed. Figure-only: `› ⇥ ⌥ ▌ ✦ ·`. Frame-only: `↑ ↓ ⎿ │` of the transcript beneath and `┃ ╽` its scrollbar

Three forms in one section: the frame's empty table is a box-less `No matches.`, the refused plot is the error box (`✗`), and the too-small frame is the plain notice; the figure's boxes carry `×`, `▲` and `●` marks (`▲ 34×8`, a stale `updated 4m ago`, an interrupted notice) that the tree's forms do not draw. A real disagreement on the too-small and stale forms, proposed as NEW-b3. Frame-only: `✗` the refusal's mark. Figure-only: `· × ▲ ●`
The frame is the `steps` kind's states (✓ ⠋ ◌ ✗). The figure draws four boxed block states (┌ ┐ └ ┘ │ ─) with ERROR banners and ✦ spinner stills; those boxes are §047's, drawn in containment.test.ts

The figure gallery draws one block of each kind with the design's sample (a braille plot with `┤`, a table with `▸ ● ✓`, an image, a form); the frame draws the framework's own fixtures of the same kinds, so the plot's axes are the closed box (`╭ ╮ ┬`) where the design draws open axes — I10, ruled and owed to b5-dpres — and the image is `▀` half blocks where the figure's is braille. Figure-only: `┼ ⠈…⣿ ▸ ● ✓ ❯ × —`. Frame-only: `… ┬ ╭ ╮ ╯ ╰ ╴ ╶ ▀`

The figure's gallery is five tool results as call entries; the frame's is the two the harness has (`/list`, `/logs`). Figure-only: `░ ▓` the query's bars and `⡀…⣿` the image result are results the harness's application does not declare. Frame-only: `⇥ ⇧ ⏎` are the footer's key hints (`⏎ send  ⇧⏎ newline  ⇥ complete`), which the framework draws and the figure's footer does not carry; `…` the truncated cell; `─ ❯` the rules and prompt

The figure is an approval whose diff overflows, bounded with `+211 more lines`; the frame is the inspection of the same condition (C23 I75, I88) in the boxed panel, bounded with a `⋯ 0 above, 24 below` row and its own `↑↓ scroll` hint. The panel versus unboxed layout is the same disagreement as §028 (NEW-b). Figure-only: `— › ← → − ⏎ ⟩`. Frame-only: `↑ ↓ ⋯ │ ┃ ┌ ┐ └ ┘ ▲`

The figure's typed-reply question floats above a live prompt with the question's detail line; the frame floats the boxed panel over the live prompt, the same §028 disagreement. Figure-only: `· › ← ↓ ⇧ − ▌ ● ⟩`. Frame-only: `• │ ┌ ┐ └ ┘ ▲`

The figure is a two-column rule table joined with ` · `; the frame draws each source beside its rendering — tab and newline shown as ⇥ and ↵, and the rendered table, patch, status and tape bringing their own marks (… ⋯ ─ │ ┌ ┐ ✗ › ⋅ ○ ✓)

The figure is an explanatory table of three identities (scroll, focus, caret) and is prose; the frame draws the property it states — the same transcript before and after the resize, whose top visible entry is unchanged. Figure-only: the em dash of the figure's prose. Frame-only: the session's own marks (`⇥ ⇧ ⎿ ⏎ ─ │ ┃ ● ❯`)

The figure is a failed tool call and a model failure; the frame draws the tool failure only. Figure-only: `—` and `←` are the design's annotations, `✦` the retry notice, a model failure being the application's. Frame-only: `⇥ ⇧ ⏎` are the footer's key hints (`⏎ send  ⇧⏎ newline  ⇥ complete`), which the framework draws and the figure's footer does not carry; `┌ ┐ └ ┘` is the framework's error box (the figure's is an open rule with `✗` beneath); `│` is the continuation gutter under `⎿`, which the registry draws blank (ruling 2, I4 — b5-dshell's lane owns the change; this entry empties when its goldens move); `❯` the echo

The figure is the agent session scrolled back with a `↓ 3 new messages ⏎` indicator; the frame draws the scrolled transcript and its bar. The `new messages` indicator is unbuilt and unspecified in any C-spec (NEW-b4). Figure-only: the figure's session chrome (`✦` model, `⎇` branch, `✎`, `»` posture) is the application's chrome, which the harness's two-line chrome does not draw; `↓` the indicator and `◻`. Frame-only: `⇥ ⇧ ⏎` are the footer's key hints (`⏎ send  ⇧⏎ newline  ⇥ complete`), which the framework draws and the figure's footer does not carry; `┃ ╽` the bar, which the figure does not draw; `│` is the continuation gutter under `⎿`, which the registry draws blank (ruling 2, I4 — b5-dshell's lane owns the change; this entry empties when its goldens move)

The figure draws one exchange at three rungs; the frame draws the failed-verb exchange at the golden's own rung (the three goldens are the three rungs). Figure-only: `▹` a reasoning head and `—`. Frame-only: `⇥ ⇧ ⏎` are the footer's key hints (`⏎ send  ⇧⏎ newline  ⇥ complete`), which the framework draws and the figure's footer does not carry; `┌ ┐ └ ┘ ✗` the error box; `─ ❯` the rules and prompt

The figure draws five labelled upper rules; the frame draws one, the app's name on the right (`Calcium`). Figure-only: `⎇ ✎ ▌ · —` are the other four labels' branch, dirty count and caret, which the harness's chrome does not compute (the label is the application's function, §069). The label's shed at 60 columns is a separate golden (`session-frame` label-shed)

Both are ground censuses over different specimens. The figure's are a diff, a context bar (█ ░ ▒ ▓), a focused row (▸), a braille plot in a well (┤ ┼ and its dots), an image (▀) and the prompt's posture (» ⏎); the frame's are a patch with its residue (⋯), a status box (┌ ┐ │ ✗), the pills posture and a plot well

The frame is §073's test run over every kind plus the button's rungs, and its ▀ is the image kind's grounded cells in that census. The figure draws buttons, titles (┌ ┐ ├ ┤ ─), widgets (○ ● ✓), a table header under ▸, and the posture (» ⏎)

The figure draws the SGR table and the tone-to-weight ladder; the frame draws the ladder (`tone  this rung  1-bit`) as words, so the figure's `· → ␛ ● ✗` marks (the escape glyph, the arrow, the 24-bit and 1-bit state dots) are not in it. The weights agree with the figure's table, which theme-tokens holds

The figure's `/config` is a table in a titled panel with a toned source column, an `⏎ edit` footer and a legend; the frame draws the panel and the table without a footer or legend, and `env`/`flag` are untoned because C04 I6 refuses a `warn` or `error` tone without a glyph. Figure-only: `— ⏎ ▸` the title rule's dash, the footer's hint and the cursor row. A real disagreement on the toning (NEW-b5)

The figure draws a token-to-tone legend and a highlighted function; the frame draws the `code` kind on the fixture's YAML, which has no `—` (the figure's legend has). The grammar is the harness's registered one, not TypeScript; colour is not compared at this rung

The figure is a sorted file table with a `▾` header mark and a `+8 more` residue; the frame is the ps table sorted by age with `▹+4` shed-column marks in every row. Figure-only: `·` and `▴`, the ascending mark the frame's descending sort does not draw. Frame-only: `▹ ●` the expand twisty and the state dot, which the figure's file table has no column for. The `+8 more` residue is not in the frame because five rows fit

The figure draws ten tone swatches and nine surface swatches; the frame prints the dark theme's values at this rung, as text, so the swatch glyphs `█ ▌` and the `–` range dash and `·` are the figure's alone. The values themselves are held by theme-tokens against the registry

The ground's extent is what the frame checks (C11 §5c, I25) and it agrees; the detail's contents are the producer's, so the figure's progress row (█ ░), action bar (≡ ⚡ ⊘) and ● ⎿ call head are specimen content the table's expansion does not carry

At 80 columns the frame's five members fit, so it draws no «n or n» and no ⋯ lead; its state marks are ⋅ (the running spinner at its tick) and ○ (queued) where the figure's are ✦ (the fixtures' still) and ✓. ⌃⇥ is the footer's switch hint, not the tape's

The frame draws the framed container alone; the figure draws three containers — framed, under a ● call head's ⎿ gutter, and bare — and the empty case. **The message's lead agrees since ruling 85** (C09 I138, F1461): both open an ERROR with ✗. The ▲ left on the figure's side is not a lead: it is the empty case's annotation, *no banner, no ▲, no red*, which names the warning mark where the mark it withholds is now ✗. ✦ is the fixtures' spinner still

The frame is the panel LAYER since ruling 87 (F1460) — a session with the completion menu open over an empty transcript — and the box marks the block kind brought are gone with the homonym. ● is the figure's reply specimen above the menu, which this frame leaves out so every mark is the layer's or the prompt's; ▌ is the figure's drawn cursor, where the tree's is the terminal's own; — is line 32's prose. **› is shared since ruling 89** (C19 I29, C11 I33, F1474): the menu's current candidate is the first at rest, drawn with `current`'s mark, the `pick` ground and the weight, and the other rows keep the mark's cells. **And the menu closes on the prompt's upper rule since ruling 90** (C19 I23, F1475): one rule under the candidates where the frame drew two stacked rows, which the marks cannot see and this frame's rows show. What the figure still draws and the frame does not: the other candidates on `bgElev`, which is not ruled
The cut ladder and the decimal columns agree in their marks; the frame's │ is the measured box's edge, and the figure's ❯ ▌ ● are the prompt and the call heads its paths sit in

The figure draws the table's shed-everything-else narrow form and a split patch; the frame draws the table at the golden's width and at 32 columns with the twisty and `▹+4`, and the split patch. Figure-only: `· −` the split's header (`− before │ + after`) which the patch kind does not draw. Frame-only: `⋯ ─` the patch's residue and rule, `▹ ●` the twisty and state dot

The figure is the question's routing table and two floating panels (a reply, and a peek) around the prompt; the frame is the chip preview above the prompt, the peek half, so the routing table, the reply and the approval are held by question-routing rows. Figure-only: `… › ← → ⏎ █ ░ ⟩ ▌` are those panels' marks. Frame-only: `⇧ ⌥ ╿ │` of the footer hint `⌥⇧↑⌥⇧↓ scroll`, which runs two chords together with no separator (NEW-b6), and `⋯` the preview's residue row
